title: Audit credit is capped, decaying and firm-gated: no audit set can eliminate smart-contract risk, and unlisted firms count for nothing
content:
A.3.2.2.1.2.2.5 computes the Audit Factor as a product across firms, `AF = Π[1 − effAuditValue × decayFactor]`, where each audit's effective value is `effectivenessCoefficient × coverage` (A.3.2.2.1.2.2.5.1). Four design choices in that expression do most of the work.

**No audit is conclusive.** The effectiveness coefficient is 0.8 for a top-tier firm and 0.5 for a mid-tier firm (A.3.2.2.1.2.2.5.1.2.1.1–.2), and coverage is `LinesOfCodeCovered / TotalLinesOfCode`. A single perfect-coverage top-tier audit therefore removes at most 80% of base risk. Zero is only approached by stacking multiple independent firms — the multiplicative form rewards diversity of reviewers over depth from one.

**Audits expire.** The decay factor is 1 for audits up to two years old, falls linearly as `(10 − auditAge)/8` between two and ten years, and is 0 at ten years or more (A.3.2.2.1.2.2.5.2). Security evidence is treated as perishable, which is correct for code whose dependencies and environment change even when it does not.

**One audit per firm.** "The audit from each audit firm with the highest product of Effective Audit Value and Delay factor should be included" — repeated engagements with the same firm do not compound. This blocks the cheapest way to inflate the factor and encodes the assumption that a firm's second look finds correlated bugs.

**Auditors are whitelisted.** A.3.2.2.1.2.2.5.1.2.2 provides that "audits from firms other than the ones specified herein may not be included," naming four top-tier firms (ChainSecurity, OpenZeppelin, ConsenSys Diligence, Trail Of Bits) and roughly thirty mid-tier ones, with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead required to "review this categorization on a regular basis."

The whitelist is the governance-heavy part: an Atlas-level list of approved vendors, maintained by a single named role, that materially determines the capital cost of every integration. It is effective against audit-shopping and creates a real barrier for new audit firms, whose work is worth exactly zero to a Prime Agent until the list is updated.
description: Effectiveness is 0.8 for top-tier and 0.5 for mid-tier firms times line-coverage, values decay to zero over ten years, only the best audit per firm counts, and the firm list is governance-maintained.
